metadata.title: [Model][SM70] DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on V100: PP3xTP4 (12 GPUs, 256K) and PP2xTP4 (8 GPUs)
metadata.body:
> Contributed by PLI Labs (Proprietary Legal Intelligence). The same branch is published at [ProprietaryLegal/1Cat-vLLM](https://github.com/ProprietaryLegal/1Cat-vLLM/tree/feat/deepseek-v41-sm70). The patch series, launch scripts, measured results and the FP32 reference tools are on Hugging Face at [ProprietaryLegal/deepseek-v4.1-flash-sm70](https://huggingface.co/ProprietaryLegal/deepseek-v4.1-flash-sm70).

## Purpose

This PR runs [deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash](https://huggingface.co/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash) on V100 from the official checkpoint, unchanged. The checkpoint has FP8 E4M3 dense weights with 32 × 32 UE8M0 scales, MXFP4 routed experts and the Engram tables. Two layouts are supported:
- 12 GPUs as PP3 × TP4, up to 256K context;
- 8 GPUs as PP2 × TP4, with part of the routed experts in pinned host memory.

The model lives in a new package, `vllm/models/deepseek_v41/`, with the SM70 code in `sm70/`. The DeepSeek-V4 files are not modified.

This PR is stacked on #1030. Its first two commits are that PR (the MXFP4 MoE geometry and the skinny split-K cases). Once #1030 merges, this diff shrinks to commits 3–5.

## What is in it

**Commit 3 — `[Core]`: three fixes that are not DeepSeek-specific.** They were carried from issue #442 work, and the V4.1 build was validated with them:
- speculative drafts are filled before the structured-output grammar bitmask;
- one faulted NVML device no longer aborts startup;
- `GPU-<uuid>` entries in `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` are kept verbatim.

Each fix has its own test. They can be split out if you prefer.

**Commit 4 — the model.**

| Area | What |
| --- | --- |
| Config / frontend | `deepseek_v41` and `deepseek_v41_text` config, with registry and quant claim. Tokenizer and chat encoding, reasoning parser and DSML tool parser are ports of upstream vLLM's V4.1 files onto 1Cat's parser bases. Streaming and non-streaming tool parsing share one acceptance rule. Also renderer registration. |
| Numerics | The hyper-connection stream is stored in BF16, with FP32 HC math (the reference's single-pass shifted pre/post) and RMSNorm eps 1e-20 in FP32. Sublayer inputs are FP16; `wo_b` and MoE outputs stay FP32. `allow_fp16_reduced_precision_reduction=False`. |
| Dense FP8 32 × 32 | Dequantised to FP16 at load through the existing SM70 fallback. This is exact for this checkpoint (scale exponents −13…−6), and every weight is checked at load. An opt-in FP8 group-32 path (TurboMind tiles + GEMV) is included but off by default. |
| Attention | Window and compressed KV are stored as FP16 records that hold the model's QAT values exactly, using bit-exact FP8/FP4 q-dq encoders. Also included: compressor ratios 1 and 2; the 32-head indexer with FP32 q; Full / Reindex / Reuse layers over kv sources 2/8/14/20; the candidate-block mask above 16K tokens; SM70 sparse MLA prefill and decode; attention sink. New KV specs and grouping for these records. |
| MoE | sqrtsoftplus router (bias used for selection only). 384 × top-6 MXFP4 experts on the skinny QPN kernels, with the TurboMind generic stages selectable. The shared expert is added in the FP32 combine. Optional spill of routed experts to pinned host memory (UVA), whose results are bitwise equal to all-resident. Decode GEMVs for K = 5120. |
| Engram (layers 1, 14) | Hashing runs on the CPU from token ids. Rows are read in place from the checkpoint shards: one aligned `pread` per 256-byte row, from a thread pool (`csrc/engram_rows.cpp`, built at runtime), into pinned staging with an async H2D copy. Rows are prefetched at admission and after sampling. The E8M0 scales are resident in pinned memory. `wkv` is row-parallel with an FP32 all-reduce. A second real forward within one step fails loudly. |
| Pipeline parallel | Only legal stage cuts are accepted: 20 for PP2; 14 and 28 for PP3. Under PP3, stage 3 holds a mirror of kv source 20, which is shipped in the PP payload with an optional CRC check. The payload is schema-driven. Worker and runner hooks carry the Engram step plan. |
| Server | An engine death now makes the API server exit non-zero; it used to exit 0. |
| Tools | `tools/bootstrap_ds41_sm70.sh` (reproducible SM70-only build) and `tools/ds41_sm70_build_smoke.sh`. |

**Commit 5.** The Engram row directory defaults to the model directory. `VLLM_DS41_CORE_ENGRAM_DIR` still overrides it, for example to put shards 47 and 48 on a faster disk.

## Test Plan

Build `_C` for `TORCH_CUDA_ARCH_LIST=7.0` (or run `tools/bootstrap_ds41_sm70.sh --execute`). Then run:

```console
pytest tests/models/deepseek_v41 tests/kernels/moe/test_sm70_mxfp4_moe_geometry.py \
       tests/v1/core/test_engine_core_structured_drafts.py tests/entrypoints/test_launcher_engine_death.py
```

Some tests need data, which they read from environment variables:

| Variable | Data |
| --- | --- |
| `DS41_CHECKPOINT_DIR` | official checkpoint |
| `DS41_GOLDEN_DIR` | golden tensors from the FP32 reference |
| `DS41_ENGRAM_DIR` | Engram shards |

When the data is absent these tests skip. The GPU tests need SM70 cards.

End to end, on 12 GPUs:

```console
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=<12 UUIDs, 4 per NVLink board> VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=14,14,12 VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=0 \
python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server --model <DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash dir> --dtype half \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --pipeline-parallel-size 3 --max-model-len 262144 --max-num-batched-tokens 4096 \
  --enable-chunked-prefill --gpu-memory-utilization 0.92 --no-async-scheduling --enforce-eager \
  --tokenizer-mode deepseek_v41 --reasoning-parser deepseek_v41 --enable-auto-tool-choice --tool-call-parser deepseek_v41
```

Engram refuses to serve rows from a shard it cannot see as verified. After checking shards 47 and 48 against the sha256 published on the Hub, write each hash into `<shard>.sha256-ok` next to the shard. `VLLM_DS41_ENGRAM_REQUIRE_VERIFIED=0` turns the check off; it is meant for tests.

For 8 GPUs, set `--pipeline-parallel-size 2`, `VLLM_PP_LAYER_PARTITION=20,20` and `VLLM_DS41_CORE_SPILL_EXPERTS_PER_LAYER=120`.

## Test Result

Hardware:
- 12 × V100-SXM2-32GB on three 4-card NVLink boards, connected board to board over PCIe only;
- SM clock capped at 1477 MHz; board power limits 265 W, 238 W and 180 W;
- Threadripper PRO 3945WX, 196 GiB RAM;
- driver 580.159.03, CUDA 12.8.93, torch 2.10.0+cu128.

Run settings: eager mode, synchronous scheduling.

**Correctness.** The reference is a pure-torch FP32 transcription of DeepSeek's `inference/` code. On a 9-layer random model it matches that code bitwise. Results:
- **Greedy.** The 32 greedy tokens of the smoke prompt equal the reference continuation.
- **Teacher-forced scoring, pooled over 4 prompts (2,419 positions):**

  | Metric (PP3 port) | Port | Reference at the port's precision (BF16 stream, FP16 inputs) |
  | --- | ---: | ---: |
  | \|ΔNLL\| | 0.0321 | 0.0335 |
  | top-1 agreement | 0.9847 | 0.9868 |
  | KL, top-20 lower bound | 0.0051 | 0.0040 |
  | \|ΔNLL\| vs the reference's own activation quantisation | 0.0435 | — |

  Every metric passes its gate. A planted bug (one Engram layer skipped) fails all of them.
- **PP3 vs PP2.** A full dump of PP3 (prefill and 3 decode steps, every layer, the logits) is bitwise identical to PP2: 2,744 tensors.
- **Mirror CRC.** No errors, including at 256K.

**Long context** (PP3, single stream, needle at 40 % depth, 256 generated tokens):

| Prompt tokens | TTFT | Prefill tok/s | Decode tok/s | Needle |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| 1,018 | 1.9 s | 537 | 2.94 | found |
| 32,745 | 16.6 s | 1,977 | 3.00 | found |
| 131,065 | 79.6 s | 1,646 | 2.46 | found |
| 261,465 | 222.8 s | 1,173 | 2.72 | found |

**Capacity and memory** (PP3):
- KV capacity: 536,631 tokens at utilisation 0.92.
- Concurrency: 4 concurrent 1K streams reach 8.8 tok/s aggregate.
- HBM peak per GPU: 31,476 / 32,004 / 28,484 MiB.

**API.** `/health`, `/v1/models`, chat and text completions, both streaming and non-streaming, and `max_tokens` / `temperature` / `top_p` all work.

**8 GPUs** (PP2, 120 experts per layer in pinned memory): decode 3.5–3.9 tok/s, the same teacher-forced numbers to 3 digits, and 32/32 greedy.

**Unit tests.**

| Run | Tree | Result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `tests/models/deepseek_v41`, on GPU | integration tree, before the last attention-golden update | 744 passed, 3 failed, 1 skipped. The 3 failures were tests calibrated on provisional goldens; they were fixed in the final tree and pass in the attention lane's run (159 passed). |
| CPU-only, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=""` | this branch | 459 passed, 329 skipped (the GPU tests), 0 failed |
| New MoE geometry tests, on GPU | this branch | 21/21 pass |
| Existing SM70 MXFP4/skinny suites, on GPU | this branch | 2 failures, identical to main: the stale factory tests that predate this work |

The branch merges into current main without conflicts. Its tree equals the validated tree merged onto main, apart from the MoE geometry test and commit 5. A full GPU suite run on this exact branch has not been done yet.

## Not done yet (honest status)

- **Decode speed is about 3 tok/s per stream.** Profiling shows it is CPU/launch-bound in eager mode:
  - about 6,000 kernel launches per pipeline stage per step;
  - about 333 ms per token across three serial stages;
  - only about 67 ms of GPU work.

  The follow-ups, in order, are: fused HC/Sinkhorn/norm kernels, decode CUDA graphs that break around Engram, async PP scheduling, and then the FP8 group-32 dense path. That work is in progress and is not part of this PR.
- **Use `--enforce-eager`.** The V4.1 attention builders declare no CUDA-graph support. Without eager mode, torch.compile fusions run, change greedy output slightly and are slower.
- **DSpark / MTP speculative decoding** is not wired up. The `mtp.*` weights are skipped at load.
- **Vision** inputs are not supported.
- **Scoring long prompts.** Teacher-forced scoring of long prompts with `prompt_logprobs` needs `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.90 --max-num-batched-tokens 1024`. The FP32 prompt logits are outside the memory profile.
- **Overlap with #1021.** If #1021 merges first, two files conflict: `sm70_884_8.cu` and `awq_sm70_gemm.cu`. Both PRs add the same group-32 E4M3 tiles; #1021 additionally rewords comments and refuses group 32 for the gated-SiLU and pre-scaled variants. Take #1021's versions of both files. V4.1 never calls those variants.

💬 Join our developer Slack at https://slack.vllm.ai to discuss your PR in `#pr-reviews`, coordinate on features in `#feat-` channels, or join special interest groups in `#sig-` channels.

PRs do not trigger a full CI run by default. Once the PR is approved and ready to go, your PR reviewer(s) can run CI to test the changes comprehensively before merging.

To run CI, PR reviewers can either: Add `ready` label to the PR or enable auto-merge.

If you have any questions, please reach out to us on Slack at https://slack.vllm.ai.

🚀

The independent structured-draft fill and UUID device-mask fixes are now integrated through #1116: https://github.com/1CatAI/1Cat-vLLM/pull/1116. The signed contribution is retained, with a compatibility guard for custom schedulers and four device-mask regressions. CPU gate: 81 passed; scoped pre-commit passed. The NVML diagnostic helper on main already covers unavailable devices, so that recovery was not duplicated. This extraction includes no DeepSeek model or MoE kernel; the remaining model integration stays tracked in this PR. End-to-end pipeline-parallel generation was not rerun locally. AI assistance was used for integration and validation.

Ancestry audit verified this live head a36df7c2239a13ae8da3f257151bdf92f335cc5f is retained in #1243 at 70bb718828f3c0620c0fb44ec5f671dd67194e47. This closure is not a main merge and does not qualify outstanding hardware/model/quality cases. Audit assisted by Codex.
